name: Postgres migration runner
purpose: The in-tree runner that reads numbered forward-only .sql files from the elicited migrations directory, applies each inside its own transaction against the elicited connection URL, and tracks applied filenames in a schema_version bookkeeping table it maintains inside the same database. The runner mode (atBoot or ciStep) is elicited on ADR-2803; the runner tool (bespoke Node runner, node-pg-migrate, sqitch, flyway) is elicited on ADR-2802; the shipped fixture provides a bespoke Node runner as the reference implementation.
responsibilities: Read the elicited migrations directory (default ./migrations/); enumerate .sql files sorted by their leading integer; reject a duplicate leading integer at load time (AC-27102-1).
Ensure the schema_version bookkeeping table exists on first invocation; upsert only via the applied-filename row it inserts on each successful file (AC-27102-1).

For each un-applied file, in order, open the per-file transaction through the BEGIN primitive owned on TAC-2803-persistence-data-postgres-transaction-helper.interfaces.withTransaction, read the file body, execute it, insert the applied-filename row into schema_version, close through the COMMIT primitive owned on the same interface (AC-27102-1).

On any statement failure inside a file's transaction, unwind through the ROLLBACK primitive owned on TAC-2803-persistence-data-postgres-transaction-helper.interfaces.withTransaction, emit migrationApplyFailed with the failing filename, stop the runner, exit non-zero (AC-27109-1).
On successful completion of every file, emit migrationsApplied with the applied-filename list.
internalStructure: One CLI-invokable Node module plus a library entry point the facade may call from atBoot mode. The module reads its config (connection URL, migrations directory, bookkeeping table name) from an elicited config source; enumerates the directory; loops over un-applied files; issues one BEGIN/apply/COMMIT per file; writes the schema_version row inside the same transaction so a mid-COMMIT crash never leaves a row behind for a file whose body did not land.

interfaces.name: run
interfaces.description: node migrate.mjs applies every un-applied file in order; exits 0 on success, non-zero on any failure with the failing filename in stderr.

interfaces.name: applyAll
interfaces.description: applyAll({ connectionUrl, migrationsDir, bookkeepingTable, onEvent }) -> Promise<{ applied: string[] }>. Library entry point the facade may call in atBoot mode.

dependencies.name: Postgres facade
dependencies.description: The runner may share the facade's connection pool in atBoot mode; in ciStep mode it opens its own pg.Client directly against the elicited URL and disposes it on exit.

tradeoffs: One file one transaction bounds the rollback surface cleanly but forbids a migration that spans two files atomically. Projects that need a schema change split across two files inside one transaction combine the change into one file. Numbered forward-only excludes down migrations by design; a rollback is a new numbered file inverting the earlier change, not a down step.
